A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SEM research work. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original CIFAR-10 non-stationarity experiments and reinforcement-learning evaluations, including learning curves, representation diagnostics, ablations and runtime measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds regularizer comparisons, layer-placement experiments, an additional Atari game and PQN evaluations.

M1.justification: The grouped-softmax mapping, objectives and recommended penultimate-layer placement remain unchanged. However, v2 Figure 2 newly depicts LayerNorm before softmax. Neither the method text nor Appendix E establishes whether this operation was introduced or merely omitted from the earlier diagram, leaving an actual procedural change unresolved.

E1.justification: Atari coverage increases from 27 to 28 games: Asteroids is added in v2 Figure 30, compared with v1 Figure 19. The other benchmark and task coverage is retained. The new PQN evaluation uses the same Atari tasks rather than introducing a new domain.

E2.justification: Appendix H substantially expands evaluated comparators with ReGen, Shrink-and-Perturb, weight clipping, resets, spectral and feature normalization, GELU, Dropout, SoftMoE/Top1-MoE, ReDo and magnitude pruning. Appendix M also adds PQN versus PQN+SEM. The original actor-critic and discrete-representation comparisons remain.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce extensive controlled settings, including one versus four MoE experts, 50% versus 95% pruning, and individual-layer versus all-layer interventions at dimensions 64 and 128. Figure 33 extends the walk/critic-rank diagnostic horizon. These additions do not establish reruns of retained experiments. The PQN aggregation scope is inconsistent: Appendix M specifies 28 games, whereas Figure 38 says 18.

E4.justification: v2 adds regularizer-strength sensitivity studies in Appendix H, a single-simplex control in Figure 34, layer-placement ablations in Figures 35–36, and an extended return/effective-rank diagnostic in Figure 33. These investigate alternative regularization mechanisms, grouping and intervention location beyond the original SEM-parameter and FastTD3-design ablations.

E5.justification: v2 newly specifies three CIFAR-10 seeds and 95% confidence intervals, identifies shaded intervals in Sections 4–5, and reports stratified-bootstrap confidence intervals for PQN in Figure 38. Existing six-seed continuous-control, three-seed Atari and five-seed OGBench counts remain unchanged; additional runs for retained experiments are not established.

E6.justification: Substantial new results accompany the regularizer comparisons, single-simplex and layer-placement tests, extended diagnostics, Asteroids evaluation and PQN experiments. Reported findings include Layer-3 performing comparably to all-layer intervention, single-simplex performance plateauing, and no consistent aggregate PQN benefit. Most earlier learning curves and all runtime values in Table 2 are retained.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 and its proof in Appendix B, the FastTD3 derivations in Appendix C, and diagnostic definitions in Appendix G are unchanged. Moving the expected-return expression inline and renumbering equations do not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and discussion retain the central contribution: lightweight simplicial representations improve actor-critic sample efficiency and final performance while preserving runtime efficiency. The abstract adds a code link but no new scientific claim; additional experiments do not redefine the headline contribution.

C2.justification: Section 4 replaces v1's interpretation that excessive L harms returns with a capacity-driven improvement-and-saturation account of the same Figure 7 curves. New discussion identifies inconsistent benefits for PQN and possible game-specific dependencies. Appendix L adds evidence-based reasoning that a penultimate-layer intervention captures most benefits of modifying every layer.

D1.justification: v2 adds a source-code link, specifies L=2 for Figure 3 and L=128, V=4 for PPO's 512-dimensional Atari representation, and explicitly depicts LayerNorm. Appendix H supplies implementation details and parameter values for the added comparators. Reproducibility documentation expands substantially, although Shrink-and-Perturb settings in the prose conflict with Figure 16's labels.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting regularization baselines, non-stationary learning and Atari evaluation, including regenerative regularization, spectral normalization, resets and statistical evaluation. Appendix A and the original positioning relative to model-based and discrete-latent approaches remain largely unchanged. Numerous publication-year and venue updates refer to existing works.

P1.justification: The main six-section narrative is retained, with localized rewrites of the capacity discussion, Atari description and discussion, plus a value-based evaluation paragraph. New appendix sections organize additional comparisons and analyses. Headers change from preprint to conference publication, and minor wording and reference corrections appear throughout.

P2.justification: The visual evidence expands substantially through new regularizer, diagnostic, single-simplex, layer-placement and PQN plots. The Atari grid gains an Asteroids panel, Figure 2 gains LayerNorm, and several captions are expanded. Existing figures and tables are largely preserved, with relocation and renumbering distinguished from these additions.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical validation by testing plausible alternative regularizers and directly examining the chosen SEM insertion layer, important gaps in v1. Negative PQN results provide a useful applicability boundary, while additional SEM settings and a code-access link improve reproducibility documentation. These gains outweigh the added reporting inconsistencies, particularly conflicting Shrink-and-Perturb settings and the 18-versus-28-game PQN aggregation description.
